title: Tiny surface fixes review scratchpad
content:
Context / quick summary:
- Working through a lightweight review pass on PR #3489 (small routing + cache-key tweaks). This is mostly surface-level but surfaced a few follow-ups that could reduce flakiness and token-cost edge cases.
- Goal: ship the PR quickly but capture follow-ups and low-risk refactors into short tickets so the main change stays small.

Top-level checklist (ship readiness):
- [ ] Tests passing locally (unit + integration)
- [x] Basic linting clean
- [ ] Add a tiny e2e that simulates prefix cache hit/miss under short TTL
- [ ] Add a perf smoke (measure tokens/sec on small sample workload)

Immediate safety notes (blocking concerns):
- Cache-key normalization change (line 92) could cause collisions between requests that differ only in header ordering. Need to confirm deterministic ordering and that we don't drop headers that matter for routing.
- Fallback path: when cache miss + slow backend, we currently do not increase request priority. This could degrade tail latency for high-SLO customers. Not a blocker for this patch but file ticket.

Tiny fixes to include in this PR (low-risk):
- Normalize header list before serializing cache key (use sorted keys). Code comment added but include a unit test.
- Add a helper in tests/utils: buildRequest({ method, headers, body }) to avoid duplicated setup.
- Replace `if (x) return;` with explicit guard + comment in handler to make reasoning easier (line ~210).

Refactor ideas (do in separate PRs; capture scope + rough steps):
1) Move cache key construction into CacheKey class (INF-xxx)
   - Rationale: centralizes normalization + makes caching easier to reason about.
   - Steps: create class, migrate current builders, add property-based tests for collision cases.
   - Risks: moderate; touches hot path. Require bench and rollout plan.

2) Small routing policy shim for customer tiers
   - Rationale: avoid polluting main router with ifs for premium vs standard.
   - Steps: add thin policy interface, wire in for two checks, add metrics.
   - Risks: low. Can canary on staging.

3) Consolidate repeated try/catch logging into `errorContext.wrap()` util
   - Rationale: reduce noisy logs and ensure consistent structured fields.
   - Steps: add util, migrate 6 callsites, validate logs in staging.
   - Risks: low. Non-invasive.

Tests to add (priority order):
- unit: cache key normalization permutations (headers order, extra whitespace, duplicates).
- integration: simulate cold start + concurrent identical requests => ensure single upstream fetch (dedupe).
- e2e: TTL expiry path that triggers fallback model variant to ensure path correctness.

Performance thoughts / bench ideas:
- Current change touches string concat in hot path. Microbench: compare old concat vs join with pre-allocated arrays for common cases. Expect small but measurable CPU/TPS improvement under very high qps.
- Run quick perf on dev-gpu-3 for 10k small requests using the harness: /infra/bench/harness. Capture tokens/sec and tail latency.

Observability / telemetry updates needed:
- Add metric: cache_key_collisions_v2 (count true collisions detected via hash mismatch).
- Tag existing cache metrics by `normalization_version` so we can compare old/new behavior for a week post-deploy.

Risk matrix (quick):
- Data correctness: medium (cache key change) — mitigate with tests and canary.
- Latency: low (string ops) — mitigated by bench + canary.
- Logs: low — no change except suggested helpers.

Communication and rollout plan:
- Merge small PR after green tests + one SRE + one reviewer sign-off.
- Create short changelog note for slack #eng-runtime: "Cache key normalization: fix header-order collisions; added tests; follow-ups: CacheKey class ticket (INF-XXXX)".
- Canary: 5% traffic for 24h, monitor cache hit ratio, 95/99 latency, and collision metric.

Notes to self / hypotheses to validate after deploy:
- Hypothesis A: Normalizing headers will reduce collision-related cache misses by ~15% on small sample of requests (customer: beta).
- Hypothesis B: String join micro-optimization will be negligible unless throughput > 5k rps per instance.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Are there customers relying on header order today? (ask Maya / support)
- Should we include header whitelist for cache keys or default to all? (tradeoff: safety vs cache miss risk)

Next actions (short):
- [ ] Add minimal unit tests for header normalization (assign: Anika, est: 2h)
- [ ] Add test util to reduce duplication (assign: Anika, est: 1h)
- [ ] Draft ticket for CacheKey class with perf checklist (assign: Samir, est: 3h)
- [ ] Post quick note in #eng-runtime with link to PR and monitoring plan (assign: Ethan, est: 30min)

Scratchpad -- quick snippets / mental bookmark:
- naive key: `${method}|${path}|${JSON.stringify(headers)}` => problem: JSON.stringify order varies
- better: `${method}|${path}|${headersSorted.map(k=>`${k}:${headers[k]}`).join('|')}`
- consider stable hash: sha256(normalized) to keep keys compact in redis

Local commands I used:
- yarn test --filter cache-key
- node scripts/bench-local.js --qps 2000 --payload small

If stuck: ping @Maya or @Samir for historical context on why we included certain headers originally.

End of scratchpad.

(Leaving this in users/ so I can scribble more as I work; will move finalized checklist to the PR description before merging.)
